title: Tactile feedback fabric: sprint readout and micro-probes
summary: Concise synthesis of customer signals gathered during Oct-Nov sprint focused on tactile runtime experience (latency spikes, KV cache behavior, and operator ergonomics). This doc surfaces recurring developer pain, three representative vignettes, prioritized micro-features, and a short list of pragmatic probes we can run next sprint.
notes: Tone: working readout for eng + product. Contains rough scoring and open questions. Not customer-facing. Collated from 8 CS interviews, 12 support threads, and two recorded pairing sessions with integrator customers.
customer_vignettes: Vignette A — 'Live-edit loop' (mid-market SaaS): Developer notices 200–400ms tail spikes every 25th request when using streaming+kv cache. They added retry logic which caused duplicate outputs in UI. Wants predictable tail latency or a way to mark idempotent repairs.

Vignette B — 'Pin-and-fallback' (enterprise fintech): Platform pinned to a quantized variant for cost; during scheduled maintenance fallback to hosted model produced different tokenization on tool calls and broke structured outputs. Wants safer fallback policy and contract for tokenizer/response shape compatibility.

Vignette C — 'Embed drift alarm' (search vendor): Batch embedding jobs occasionally return outlier vectors triggering downstream reindex jobs to fail; customer suspects transient GPU kernel mismatch during autoscale events and asks for batch-level checksum / sample echoes.
prioritized_requests: 1) 'Fallback contracts' — define and surface per-model compatibility matrix (tokenizer, function-call schema, stop-sequences). Priority: P0 for Dedicated/Private customers with strict contracts.
2) 'KV cache health' — lightweight KV cache diagnostic endpoint + per-customer cache hit histogram visible in Console (last 24h). Priority: P1 across hosted + dedicated.
3) 'Streaming tail SLO' — allow route-level SLO override that forces smaller batching windows for latency-sensitive routes (opt-in). Priority: P1.
4) 'Batch checksum/echo' — optional sampling mechanism that returns a deterministic short digest of input batch so integrators can detect drift post-deploy. Priority: P2.
5) 'Dry-run traffic replay' — UI/CLI tool to replay a sample of production traffic against candidate model variants without affecting live KV caches. Priority: P2.
6) 'Token-cost ledger per-example' — expose an approximate per-call token cost in trace detail for top 50 routes; customers ask to attribute cost to product features. Priority: P3.
quick_fixes: Expose 'force-compat' flag in API gateway to prefer model variants that preserve tokenizer/func-call shapes (engineering config only). Est. effort: ~3 dev days, rollout as warning flag.
Add a console toggle to disable prefix caching per-route (useful for debugging streaming duplication). Est. effort: 2 dev days + 1 QA day.
Add a support-runbook snippet that walks CS through diagnosing embedding drift: check autoscale events, kernel-version mapping, and run sample-echos. Est. effort: 1 doc day.
Implement a low-sampling 'batch-digest' header on batch inference responses to detect silent mismatches. Est. effort: 4 dev days.
Add a Canary checklist item: run a 1k-example dry replay after model promotion. Est. effort: procedural change only.
cost_latency_tradeoffs: Customers repeatedly trade lower unit-cost (quantized models and aggressive batching) for stability and deterministic behavior. Proposed pattern: expose a simple 'cost-mode' profile (economy | balanced | predictable) per-route with documented implications (batch sizes, fallback tolerance, KV cache wildcarding). Engineering note: predictable mode disables certain kernel-level quantization paths and reduces batch window — increases $/token ~ 15–40% depending on workload.
probed_hypotheses: H1: Tail spikes correlate with autoscale pod rotations causing temporary kernel mismatch when KV cache is warm. Quick probe: correlate tail-latency spikes with node-restart events in last 30 days.
H2: Duplicate outputs on streaming are caused by concurrent prefix-cache invalidation + client reconnect. Quick probe: instrument connection lifecycle in streaming layer for top 3 customers.

H3: Embedding outliers are reproducible with identical binary + quantization but non-deterministic under different CUDA/driver versions. Quick probe: run deterministic embedding test across nodes with pinned driver versions.
H4: Developers want replay tooling more than full-featured rollout UI; a lightweight CLI for dry-run replay will get faster adoption. Quick probe: ship alpha CLI and measure usage in 2 customers.
H5: Visible per-example cost attribution for top routes reduces billing disputes and helps customers optimize prompts. Quick probe: add cost column to tracing UI for Beta customers.
open_questions: Q1: If we add 'predictable' route mode that disables certain quantized kernels, what fraction of existing hosted capacity will be affected? Need capacity model from infra.
Q2: What legal/SLAs implications when we offer 'force-compat' fallback policy that may return higher-cost model variants during outages? Product/legal to advise.
Q3: Can we implement batch-digest without leaking PII or sensitive tokens? Security review required for digest design (hashing/salting scheme).
Q4: What is acceptable sampling rate for batch checksum from customer perspective (0.1% vs 5%)? CS to poll top 6 customers.
Q5: Is there appetite to surface driver/kernel versions in Console? Operationally useful but may add support burden.
